1045.title: Isolation Fault (ISO-F)
1045.description: Ground isolation resistance of the PV array is below the safe operational threshold.
1045.oem_definition: PV Insulation Resistance Protection (ISO-PRO01 / IGF012). The insulation resistance between the PV array conductors and earth ground is lower than the inverter safety limit.
potential_causes: Damage to DC cable insulation or conduit
Water ingress or moisture inside MC4 connectors or junction boxes
Pinched module wiring against mounting rails
Degraded solar module backsheet insulation
1045.recommended_action: Perform insulation resistance testing on DC array cables and panels per Solis service manual. Check for moisture ingress.

general_field_guidance.instruction: Adhere strictly to site safety rules. De-energize AC circuit breaker and DC isolators before opening array enclosures.
Visually inspect DC cable runs, MC4 connectors, and array grounding bonds for physical chafing, damage, or water ingress.
Isolate PV strings and measure string insulation resistance to earth ground using an approved insulation tester per OEM procedures.
Repair or replace damaged cable/connector, confirm isolation resistance returns above safe limit, and verify clear status upon restart.

1021.title: Inverter Over Temperature (OV-TEMP)
1021.description: Internal inverter or heatsink temperature exceeds maximum safety limits.
1021.oem_definition: Internal Over-Temperature Protection (TEMP-PRO01). Internal inverter or heatsink operating temperature has exceeded the thermal protection limit.
potential_causes: Dust, dirt, or debris clogging external heatsink cooling fins
Internal or external cooling fan obstruction or failure
Insufficient ventilation clearance around inverter enclosure
Direct ambient solar thermal exposure without adequate shading
1021.recommended_action: Verify inverter is installed in a well-ventilated location. Clean heatsink fins and inspect cooling fans.

general_field_guidance.instruction: Exercise caution near inverter enclosure. Verify heatsink casing temperature is safe to touch before servicing.
Inspect external heatsink fins for accumulation of dirt, debris, bird nests, or airflow blockages.
Check cooling fan rotation and verify ambient installation clearances match minimum OEM installation specifications.
Clean heatsink fins using soft brush/compressed air, restore cooling airflow, and verify temperature drop on display/telemetry.

1011.title: Grid Over Voltage (OV-G-V)
1011.description: The utility grid voltage exceeds the inverter's maximum allowed limit.
1011.oem_definition: Grid Over-Voltage Protection (OV-G-V / OV-V01). Utility AC grid voltage exceeds the inverter grid standard threshold.
potential_causes: Utility grid AC voltage surge or local grid fluctuation
High AC line impedance or loose AC terminal connections causing local voltage rise
Undersized AC cabling between inverter and main grid tie panel
1011.recommended_action: Inverter will auto-reconnect once grid voltage stabilizes. Contact grid provider if high voltage persists.

general_field_guidance.instruction: Observe AC electrical safety precautions when inspecting main AC distribution equipment.
Inspect AC circuit breaker and AC terminal block for signs of loose connections or thermal stress.
Measure AC line-to-neutral and line-to-line voltage at inverter AC terminals using a calibrated True-RMS meter.
If grid voltage is within normal range, verify inverter grid standard settings match local utility requirements.

1012.title: Grid Under Voltage (UN-G-V)
1012.description: The utility grid voltage is lower than the inverter's minimum operational limit.
1012.oem_definition: Grid Under-Voltage Protection (UN-G-V / UN-V01). Utility AC grid voltage is below the inverter operational minimum threshold.
potential_causes: Utility grid brownout or regional power outage
Tripped AC main breaker or blown AC fuses
Loose or disconnected AC phase connections
1012.recommended_action: Check if AC breaker is tripped. Verify utility grid connection is active.

general_field_guidance.instruction: Verify AC breaker status before attempting any panel access.
Check AC main breaker, fuses, and utility disconnect switch position.
Measure incoming utility AC voltage to confirm whether outage is site-wide or localized.
Reset AC breaker if safely permitted, and monitor inverter auto-reconnect sequence.

1015.title: Grid Over Frequency (OV-G-F)
1015.description: Grid frequency exceeds the inverter's maximum allowed limit.
1015.oem_definition: Grid Over-Frequency Protection (OV-G-F). Utility grid AC frequency exceeds upper safety boundary.
potential_causes: Utility grid frequency instability or generator supply frequency mismatch
1015.recommended_action: Inverter will auto-reconnect once grid frequency returns to normal.

general_field_guidance.instruction: No immediate physical contact required; grid frequency is managed by utility operator.
Observe inverter status indicator LED or display screen.
Check telemetry logs or grid meter for AC frequency readings.
Inverter will auto-reconnect when grid frequency recovers within statutory window.

CLEANING_OVERDUE.title: Cleaning Overdue
CLEANING_OVERDUE.description: Soiling accumulation exceeds cycle threshold, causing generation drop.
CLEANING_OVERDUE.oem_definition: Site Maintenance Alert. Module cleaning cycle interval elapsed.
potential_causes: Dust, soiling, pollen, or environmental residue on glass surface

general_field_guidance.instruction: Review site working at height / roof access safety rules.
Inspect solar module glass for dust accumulation layer, bird droppings, or soiling lines.
Perform dry or wet cleaning per site module manufacturer cleaning recommendations.
Log cleaning completion with before/after photos and update last cleaned date.
